document.title: Strategy / U.S. Strategy in Afghanistan (Rumsfeld to Feith, with NSC attachment)
document.authors: Office of the Secretary of Defense (Rumsfeld) / National Security Council
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), New Documents Detail America's Strategic Response to 9/11
document.note: [Secret/Close Hold/Draft for Discussion] NSC outlines U.S. strategy five weeks after 9/11: destroy al-Qaeda and the Taliban without committing to post-Taliban military involvement, use any Afghan tribes and factions, insert CIA teams and special forces in the north and south, and engage Pakistan, Iran and Russia. Includes a handwritten Rumsfeld note.

events.description: Rumsfeld sends edits of the 'U.S. Strategy in Afghanistan' draft to Feith and proposes sending it to the Vice President, Powell, Rice and Tenet.
Draft paper 'U.S. Strategy in Afghanistan' (7:43 AM) setting goals vs al-Qaida and the Taliban, use of Afghan factions, CIA/SF teams, Kabul and Southern tribes policy.
Rumsfeld sends Feith edits to the draft 'U.S. Strategy in Afghanistan' paper (dated 7:43 AM) and a draft memo for Cheney, Powell, Rice and Tenet.
Draft strategy sets goals to eliminate Al-Qaida leadership and terminate Taliban rule, using Afghan factions, CIA/Special Forces teams and air power.

relationships.detail: Rumsfeld, as Secretary, authored the memo and strategy paper from DoD (inferred from OSD origin).
relationships.quote: Donald Rumsfeld ... TO: Doug Feith

relationships.detail: Al-Qaida is treated as sheltered by the Taliban regime, which uses Afghanistan as a sanctuary for terrorism.
relationships.quote: End the use of Afghanistan as a sanctuary for terrorism.

relationships.detail: The Taliban rule Afghanistan; the US goal is to terminate their rule.
relationships.quote: Terminate the rule of the Taliban and their leadership.

relationships.detail: DoD and CIA are to coordinate closely to engage all Afghan factions against Al-Qaida and Taliban using incentives and disincentives.
relationships.quote: DoD and CIA coordinate closely in getting all factions engaged in eliminating Al-Qaida and Taliban

relationships.detail: CIA/DoD teams are to work with Afghan forces, primarily Northern Alliance in the north, providing money, supplies and equipment.
relationships.quote: CIA and DoD teams on the ground are critical for success-U.S. influence, targeting, logistics and humanitarian efforts.

relationships.detail: Additional CIA teams and Special Forces A teams are to be inserted in-country together, North and South.
relationships.quote: Urgently insert additional CIA teams and Special Forces in country operational ... (A teams), by any means, both in the North and the South.

relationships.detail: Northern Alliance forces are to be supported to eliminate Taliban resistance and take Kabul.
relationships.quote: Providing additional conventional support to Northern Alliance forces north of Kabul ... may set conditions for Northern Alliance to eliminate Taliban resistance in Kabul and take the city.

relationships.detail: Northern Alliance forces are north of Kabul in the vicinity of Panshir and the Shomali plains.
relationships.quote: Northern Alliance forces north of Kabul (the vicinity of Panshir and the Shomali plains)

relationships.detail: Northern Alliance forces are positioned in the Shomali plains.
relationships.quote: (the vicinity of Panshir and the Shomali plains)

relationships.detail: Afghan forces in the north are urged to establish a land bridge to Uzbekistan.
relationships.quote: Establish a land bridge to Uzbekistan by attacking and occupying land and major cities.

relationships.detail: CINCENT will use all capabilities, including air attack, to encourage and support Afghan ground forces.
relationships.quote: CINCENT will use all capabilities to encourage ground forces to achieve U.S. goals

relationships.detail: Taliban control Kabul and other key cities that the US wants them pushed out of.
relationships.quote: The sooner the Taliban is pushed out of Kabul, Herat, Mazar-e-Sharif, and other key cities, the better.

relationships.detail: Taliban hold Herat.
relationships.quote: pushed out of Kabul, Herat, Mazar-e-Sharif

relationships.detail: Taliban hold Mazar-e-Sharif.
relationships.quote: pushed out of Kabul, Herat, Mazar-e-Sharif

relationships.detail: The Northern Alliance is characterised as Tajik-Uzbek, feared by Pashtuns.
relationships.quote: relieve Pashtun fear of domination by Northern Alliance (Tajik-Uzbek) tribes.

relationships.detail: Engaging UN diplomacy beyond general outline could interfere with US military operations.
relationships.quote: Engaging U.N. diplomacy beyond intent and general outline could interfere with U.S. military operations and inhibit coalition freedom.

relationships.detail: Pakistan could help balance gains by the Northern Alliance in the South.
relationships.quote: Pakistan could be key in this regard, particularly if the U.S. emphasizes to them that this is the key to balancing gains by the Northern Alliance.

relationships.detail: King Zahir Shah may have influence with Pashtuns, especially if seen to have US confidence.
relationships.quote: The U.S. should explore the value of ties with King Zahir Shah. He may have some influence with Pashtuns

relationships.detail: Iran is described as backing Shia, feared by Pashtuns.
relationships.quote: given Pashtun fear of domination by Iranian-backed Shia.

relationships.detail: NATO allies are suggested as part of a volunteer international peacekeeping force for Kabul, not the US.
relationships.quote: ad hoc collection of volunteer states (such as Turkey, and Egypt, along with other NATO allies), but not the U.S.

relationships.detail: An international UN-based group could provide follow-on peacekeeping for Kabul.
relationships.quote: An international group could be UN-based or an ad hoc collection of volunteer states

relationships.detail: US suggests encouraging the Taliban to surrender Kabul without Northern Alliance forces needing to take it by force.
relationships.quote: It may be wise to encourage the Taliban to surrender the city without the Northern Alliance forces having to invest and occupy it by force

relationships.detail: The President prepared the public for a long campaign against Taliban/Al Qaida.
relationships.quote: The President has properly prepared the American public for a long campaign.

key_claims: US strategy aims to eliminate al-Qaida leadership and terminate Taliban rule while ending Afghanistan's use as terrorist sanctuary.
The US plans to use any and all Afghan tribes and factions, with CIA and Special Forces teams, to destroy al-Qaida and Taliban personnel.
Northern Alliance is to be supported with air strikes and supplies, but US wants a political process and international force for Kabul to relieve Pashtun fear of Tajik-Uzbek domination.
Pakistan is seen as potentially key to establishing contacts with Southern Pashtuns to balance Northern Alliance gains.
The US should explore ties with King Zahir Shah but be wary of association with Russia and Iran.
The US should not commit to post-Taliban military involvement and should avoid UN diplomacy that hampers military operations.
